campaigns.title: Help Leena in saving girls from being lost forever in red-light areas
campaigns.description: "Hundreds of young girls are lost forever in the dark lanes of red-light areas," says Leena Kejriwal, the founder of Missing Link Trust. These girls endure unimaginable abuse and exploitation, being lured or trafficked into an industry that breaks them physically and emotionally. Missing Link Trust is on a mission to prevent the tragedy before it happens, and also rehabilitate girls and women who are rescued from forced sex work.Leena’s journey began with her powerful street art project in Kolkata, where she painted haunting silhouettes of missing girls to raise awareness against sex trafficking. Now, she leads a larger fight — one that focuses on prevention and rehabilitation. But this mission needs your support.You can save countless girl children from going missing forever. Donate now.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).Preventing Trafficking Before It Begins“When girls come into a red-light area, the first thing is that they are broken, physically and emotionally,” Leena says. “It’s like they will be caught, hands and legs tied, and all heinous crimes committed on them.” These are the brutal realities that Missing Link Trust fights against every day.Many of these girls are from impoverished regions like the Sundarbans, and traffickers prey on their vulnerability. “It’s shocking that they sell themselves for as low as a hundred rupees,” Leena adds. "They ready her through violent acts, removing all threads of shame from her."But why wait until a girl is trafficked to save her? Missing Link Trust believes in stopping trafficking at its root — through “prevention, prevention, prevention” as Leena puts it. The goal is simple: protect girls from ever being lost to this darkness.A Safe World for Children“Our mission is the prevention of abuse and exploitation of children,” Leena emphasizes. “Our vision is to create a safe world for children, and we want to do this with a preventive methodology.”Every Donation MattersYour support will help Missing Link Trust continue its vital work of rescuing, rehabilitating, and preventing the trafficking of young girls. The funds raised will go directly towards:Prevention programs in vulnerable areas to stop trafficking before it happens.Rehabilitation services for girls rescued from red-light areas, providing them with medical care, emotional support, and education.Awareness campaigns to reach at-risk communities and ensure girls are protected from traffickers.Together, We Can Make a Difference“Why wait for a girl to get trafficked to save her?” asks Leena. With your help, we can stop this horror before it begins. Your donation will help us create a world where no girl is lost to the nightmare of trafficking.Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s largest and most trusted online giving platform, to support Missing Link Trust to save young girls from being trafficked and help rehabilitate those rescued.

campaigns.title: This Pitru Paksha, help feed warm meals to abandoned elderly and the destitute
campaigns.description: For thousands of elderly people, homeless individuals, daily-wage workers and vulnerable families, hunger is not an occasional hardship, it is a daily reality. Danirasa Foundation’s with the help of kind supporters and donors is quietly changing this reality for hundreds each day. Your donation provides a warm meal to an elderly grandparent who has no other means to survive. Donate Now.At ₹25 per meal, your donation of ₹1250 can cover one meal each for 50 elders, for a single day!Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking.Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).From one crisis to a mission against hungerDanirasa Foundation’s journey began during the devastating 2015 Chennai floods. Founder Indu Priya witnessed families, especially women and children, struggling with displacement and hunger. She and her team mobilised volunteers to cook and distribute hot meals. What began as an emergency response became a lasting commitment to ensuring vulnerable communities have access to food with dignity and care.Today, Danirasa’s Community Kitchen serves around 4,900 people through this programme. The meals reach elderly residents in old-age homes, children from underserved communities, rehabilitation centres, homeless people, daily-wage workers and others facing food insecurity.A meal can mean so much moreFor an elderly person living without family support, a nutritious meal can bring comfort. For someone surviving on irregular daily wages, it can mean one less worry. For a vulnerable child, it can provide the nourishment needed to learn and grow.But feeding thousands of people every day requires a steady supply of ingredients, cooking, packaging, transportation and dedicated people.Help serve a meal with dignityYour donation can help Danirasa continue providing nutritious meals to homeless and elderly people, children, workers, persons with disabilities and families struggling to make ends meet.Help Danirasa ensure that no vulnerable person has to face the day with an empty stomach. Donate today.Donate to this fundraiser by give.do, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Danirasa Foundation, in its mission to feed helpless elderly and destitute people, who have no means of survival.

campaigns.title: Help marginalized children claim a seat in the AI world
campaigns.description: Why we exist?Every technological revolution brings in progress, but not equally for everyone.The marginalized communities are often left to settle for entry-level jobs that are exploitative and prone to automation. They have limited voice on which problems get solved on priority. And the biases in society get embedded in and amplified through new technologies.How are we solving for it?Technology is power. Teaching it to marginalized children will help them claim a seat on the table. But in order for them to make right use of that power and steer technology towards creating an egalitarian world, we also need to build their character.So, teaching AI only through a technical lens is not sufficient. A holistic approach involves children understanding how it works, how it affects society and how to critically evaluate it.At THE labs, we try to do this through 3 interventions -AI Citizenship ProgramA 100-hour interdisciplinary program for middle-schoolers that aims to develop:Foundational understanding of all kinds of AI systemsAbility to critically evaluate AI systems for their impact on societyConfidence to adapt to various kinds of AI systems in the futureFellowship ProgramA 2-year residential program to prepare rural youth to be future educators and leaders in AI space by:Learning AI, Pedagogy, and LeadershipTeaching the AI Citizenship to children in government and aided schools.Developing a strong understanding of Indian social landscapeCentre of ExcellenceA community centre at Nanded City, Pune, that serves three main purposes -Opportunities for children to demonstrate their holistic learningResearch and development of new cutting-edge programsSafe space for children beyond school to spend time meaningfullyOur outreach in the current yearWe are working with more than 4000 children in urban, rural and tribal areas across 4 districts through 10 fellows, thanks to generous individuals like you who supported us last year.Read our annual impact reportWatch our children talking about their learnings and debating in classroomListen to our student sharing her research at an international conferenceTo expand this work further, we need your support!Our askDonate in this crowdfunding campaign. Below is how your donations will help us.INR 3,000 - Sponsor AI Citizenship Program for 1 child for a yearINR 15,000 - Sponsor AI Citizenship Program for 5 children for a yearINR 30,000 - Sponsor one month of a fellow's leadership journeyINR 50,000 - Sponsor one laptop that will be used by 400 children over 5 yearsTHE labs is the first organization in India to build a holistic AI program for children in grade 6 to 8. By donating any amount of your wish, you will join a community of more than 250 incredible supporters and become a pioneer in helping marginalized children claim a seat in the AI driven world.

campaigns.title: Help 70 children learn for a full year this Daan Utsav
campaigns.description: Hi, I am Shrey Rawat, and I run SURAAH, two alternative schools serving village children in the hills of Uttarakhand.Next academic year, 340 children will learn with us.This Daan Utsav, from 2 to 8 October, I am aiming to raise Rs 25 lakh to support 70 of them.An ANI documentary that captures what learning at SURAAH looks like, through someone else's eyes: children investigating the monsoon, playing football, visiting a science centre, explaining ideas to their classmates.This is what an ordinary day at SURAAH looks like.Srishti spreads ash on a garden bed while other children dig.Our children learn by doing, asking, making, exploring and engaging with the world around them. Classrooms often spill into gardens, fields, villages and the hills we live in.Children plant rice seedlings in a flooded field.Aman, blindfolded, stacks wooden blocks while his classmate watches.Grade 5 class under a tree, with the board reads "Listen, Think, Curious".What can your contribution make possible?There are many ways to stand behind our children.Rs 5,000 pays for a year of sports and games at one of our schools.Rs 20,000 pays for a year of exposure visits for one school.Rs 35,000 pays for one child to learn for a full year.Rs 1 lakh buys library books and shelving for our second school.Rs 3 lakh sets up the science lab at our second school.Reena ma'am talks through a reflection worksheet, "What do we think?"This Daan Utsav, I don’t just want to ask. I want to give.SURAAH’s Founders Collective changed what was possible for us. Today, 63 early believers have committed between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 15 lakh over three years. That gave us the stability to keep building.Now I want to give that learning forward.SURAAH’s Founders at an annual retreat at the school campus.For every Rs 5 lakh we raise for SURAAH’s children, I will make the space to handhold one young nonprofit, 0 to 3 years old, to build its own Founders Collective.At Rs 25 lakh, that means five nonprofits.The money you give supports our children. What I give is my time and what we have learnt along the way.Love,Shrey RawatFounder, SURAAH

campaigns.title: STEM at Your Doorstep: Daan Utsav 2026 Scholarship Drive
campaigns.description: Komal's parents run a small ironing stall in Dehradun. Neither of them learned to read the mathematics their daughter was falling in love with. She enrolled in B.Sc. Mathematics at DAV PG College because it was close, and because it was what the family's finances allowed. IIT was not a word anyone used at home. She had never let herself imagine it.Then a mentor from VigyanShaala started asking her a different question. Not what can you afford, but what are you capable of. He pointed her toward an internship at the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, then toward the IIT JAM exam. She cleared it. She left for Mumbai, against every instinct a childhood of scarcity had trained into her family. She earned her master's in mathematics from IIT Bombay. Today she works as a BI Developer at Axis Mutual Fund.Nothing about Komal's story was inevitable. The talent was always there. What was missing was money, at a specific point, for a specific thing, an exam fee, a train ticket, a year's tuition. When our generous partners  came with scholarships for her, we now reach thousands of students a year.She is not alone in this. Garima started in a small Himalayan town called Berinag, and went on to postgraduate studies in biotechnology, now researching frontiers of science. Tarun grew up in a village in Pithoragarh where nobody had heard of IIT JAM, and this year placed All India Rank 3 in CUET PG Chemistry. Muralika grew up in a fishing village on the Kerala coast, her father a fish vendor, and is now studying applied mathematics at the Technion in Israel. Different states, different subjects, the same pattern. Ability that was always there, waiting on something else to arrive.STEM at your doorstep is what VigyanShaala tries to build, mentoring, hands-on learning, and a path from a village school to a research lab, wherever a student happens to start. This Daan Utsav, we are asking for the one part we cannot build ourselves: the money that turns a year of possibility into a year that actually happens.Every rupee raised goes into a scholarship pool, not into running our programs. It funds students directly, at whichever stage they need it:A monthly stipend, ₹1,000, for a student in a last-mile Himalayan village or a rural pocket in Telangana.Exam preparation, ₹8,000, for a student attempting IIT JAM or CUET PG.A year's internship stipend, ₹24,000, for a Rural STEM Champions fellow from a last-mile Himalayan college.A year on a STEM project with a global mentor, ₹45,000.A full masters degree in India, ₹2,00,000, tuition and accommodation included, the tier that matches a year like Komal's. This campaign aims to raise 25 lakhs for student scholarships. We are not asking you to save anyone. Komal saved herself. Garima, Tarun, and Muralika did too. We are asking whether you want to be part of the year they couldn't have paid for on their own.

campaigns.title: गाँव लौटना बुरा नहीं | Support those who stayed. Support those who came back.
campaigns.description: गाँव लौटना बुरा नहींFrom the Ground: A Teacher Who Chose to StayNirmala teaches at the small government school in Neran, Mandi, a village she married into, after her in-laws refused to let her study further. Her husband told her something that changed her path: "If you want to serve the country, start with the children of your own village."She joined the school. Today, 22 children study there, including her own daughter. In 2023, a landslide damaged the school building, and it has never been repaired. The children's toilet is 200 metres away; every trip is a 20 minutes rough terrain walk from home. Parents now ask her one question before enrolling their child: "You don't have a building?" Enrolment keeps falling.She nearly left. Her husband and school staff talked her out of it. Instead, she chose to keep teaching, in whatever space the village could give her.She is not the only one. Across Himachal Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, 345 + youth Leaders are doing exactly this, staying back in their own villages, working out of whatever room, hall or community space is available, to keep their government schools and community specs alive which makes the villages still relevant. Nirmala is one of them.The Wrong Idea We Carry: Leaving = SuccessWe have all absorbed one idea without questioning it: the ones who leave the village are the successful ones, and the ones who stay or return are the ones who couldn't make it elsewhere.This idea is quietly dangerous, and nowhere more than in a place like Mandi. Nearly 46% of local youth migrate long-term from this district far above the national average of 29%. At the same time, government schools here are losing children. Enrolment fell by nearly 13% in just two years, even as families themselves keep saying, in effect, "there's nothing worth staying for here."But when a landslide hits, or a flash flood cuts off a hamlet and between June and September 2025 alone, Mandi lost close to ₹4,000 crore to exactly such disasters it is never the ones who left who show up first. It is the ones who stayed. Nirmala's own school sits on land that a landslide already damaged. The first people to notice a cracking slope, a rising stream, a child who has stopped coming to class, are always the people who never left.So when we say गाँव लौटना बुरा नहीं, we are correcting a wrong idea, not defending a compromise. Returning to your village, and staying rooted in it, is not settling for less. In a place as fragile and as full of potential as Mandi, it may be the most important thing a young person can choose to do.Why the Ones Who Return Need a BackerComing back and staying is hard, unpaid, often invisible work and it is bigger than any one classroom.Nirmala's story is really a story about a whole system that needs rebuilding, piece by piece, by people who belong to it. That is exactly what this work is built around not one activity in isolation, but a full, connected effort:Better government school classrooms the kind of print-rich, engaging spaces where children like Nirmala's 22 students actually want to beReal system change in the school not just events, but sustained support to local school staff like Nirmala herselfA community of local youth so no single leader is working aloneStronger parent–school connection rebuilding the trust that a missing building can break in a seasonMore participation in Gram Sabha so village decisions include the people they affectAccountability from the Panchayat so basic infrastructure requests don't disappearSkill-based learning in government schools so children graduate ready, not just promotedLiving village libraries spaces where grandparents' knowledge and children's curiosity can actually meetBreaking Gender Stereotypes Through SportsThis is not charity for one school. It is the work of creating a community of young people who are choosing to return and who need real backing to lead change that actually lasts.What Your Backing Will DoWhen you back a leader like Nirmala, you are not funding a single repair or a one-day drive. You are funding the everyday work of someone who decided to stay:Support a Local Youth Leader to Lead ChangeYour support helps young leaders like Nirmala continue creating change in their own villages through monthly mentorship, capacity building, learning spaces, resources, and a strong peer community.₹2,500 — Mentor support for one youth leader for a month₹4,500 — Learning space and resources for youth leaders for a month₹9,000 — Supports one youth leader to lead community development for a month₹1,50,000 — One capacity-building training for the entire youth leader communitEvery rupee moves a village a little further from needing outside rescue, and a little closer to leading its own resilience in the classroom, on the slope, in the Gram Sabha, and in the library.HOW MANY CONTRIBUTIONS WILL MAKE A DIFFERENCE₹2500 - 144  Hope Partners      ₹4500 - 100    Hope Partners₹9000 – 84  Hope Partners       ₹1.5L - 2  Hope PartnersYour Turn: Be the BackerNirmala did not wait for a new building to start believing in her school. She started with the children she had, in the room she had, and asked for the right kind of support to keep going.This Daan Utsav, be the backer of belonging for Nirmala, and for the community of young people across Mandi who are choosing to come home and lead.गाँव लौटना बुरा नहीं. Support those who stayed. Support those who came back.

campaigns.title: Help abandoned elderly with shelter and care
campaigns.description: Every day, elderly parents are left alone on the streets, at train stations, or even outside temples. Many are sick, struggling with age-related problems, and have no money or family to turn to. Some suffer for weeks or months before anyone notices their pain. The heartbreaking truth? They were abandoned by their own families.Although Indian law requires children and relatives to care for senior citizens, many elders still face neglect, abuse, and abandonment. The problem is only getting worse.But there is hope. Our dedicated NGO partners work day and night to rescue these forgotten elders. They provide safe shelter, medical care, nutritious meals, and most importantly—love and respect. Through old age homes across the country, our partners give these seniors a chance to live their remaining years with dignity, comfort, and peace.You can make a difference. Your donation will help our NGO partners:Rescue homeless elders from the streetsProvide shelter, food, and medical careRestore their faith in humanity with kindness and supportNo elder should spend their final years alone and suffering. Your generosity can give them a fresh start. Donate today and help an abandoned senior citizen find safety, care, and hope.

campaigns.title: Pre-School Education and Nutrition for Under 5 Year  Tribal Children
campaigns.description: GIVE India – Dan Utsav Fundraising Campaign Story₹12 a Day Can Nourish a ChildhoodStrengthening Early Childhood Nutrition & Pre-School Education in Tribal Kandhamal, OdishaIn the remote tribal villages of Kandhamal, childhood begins amid beautiful forests, hills and strong community traditions. But for many families, everyday life is shaped by poverty, food insecurity and limited access to nutritious food and early childhood learning opportunities.Many families in the proposed intervention villages earn less than ₹100 per day. For young children, this economic hardship can translate into inadequate nutrition, low immunity and challenges to healthy cognitive development.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…Kandhamal Zilla Sabuja Vaidya Sangathan (KZSVS) has worked with marginalized and tribal communities in Odisha since 2004, with programmes covering health, nutrition, education, sustainable livelihoods and natural-resource management. Today, KZSVS works across more than 600 villages, particularly with vulnerable communities, women and children.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…A programme that communities already know and trustFor the past five years, KZSVS has operated six Pre-School Education and Nutrition Centres with support from Jiv Daya Foundation. These centres have provided basic pre-school education, daily nutritional supplementation, and awareness on hygiene and health. With the earlier donor support completed, sustaining these centres has become an urgent priority.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…Through the GIVE India Dan Utsav Campaign, we are seeking the support of individual donors, friends, institutions and well-wishers to continue this journey for 250 children aged 0–5 years from six tribal villages of Kandhamal.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…The six centres are located in Tembuli, Alimaha, Breakamala, Dabedi, Petumaha and Katedimaha.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…Your ₹12 can make a differenceThe programme has been designed around a simple and achievable contribution:₹12 can support one child's nutrition for a day.₹300 can support one child for a month.₹3,600 can support one child for an entire year.₹9,00,000 can support the planned nutrition programme for 250 children for one year.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…The support will contribute to daily milk powder and biscuits, regular pre-school learning sessions, growth monitoring, basic health awareness, and engagement with parents and the wider community on child nutrition.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…More than a nutrition programmeKZSVS's approach is to place children at the centre of a stronger village ecosystem. Our experience tells us that a child's wellbeing cannot be separated from the wellbeing and resilience of their family and community.Alongside the child-focused intervention, KZSVS's wider community-development efforts include women's empowerment and livelihoods, livelihoods for persons with disabilities, WASH, rural solar electrification, agriculture, village infrastructure, community participation, cultural revival and strengthening traditional food systems.This broader approach is intended to build community ownership, rather than creating long-term dependence on external assistance. The concept note specifically envisages community contribution and ownership, stronger involvement of local SHGs, convergence with ICDS/Anganwadi services, and partnerships for long-term sustainability.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…What we hope to achieveWith sustained support, the programme seeks improved nutritional intake, reduced undernutrition and related health concerns, better cognitive and physical development, improved school readiness, and stronger community awareness of child nutrition.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…The programme will also track attendance and nutrition distribution monthly, periodically monitor children's growth, undertake field reviews, and document progress and impact stories.  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…This Dan Utsav, give a child a stronger beginningA contribution does not have to be large to matter.₹12 can begin with one child, for one day.When many people come together, those small contributions can help keep a nutrition centre running, support a child's learning, strengthen parents' awareness and give an entire community greater confidence to protect its children's future.We invite you to join KZSVS through the GIVE India Dan Utsav Fundraising Campaign and stand with the children and tribal communities of Kandhamal.Give Nutrition. Give Learning. Give Opportunity. Give a Brighter Childhood.Campaign Goal: ₹9,00,000 | Children: 250 | Villages: 6 | Pre-School & Nutrition Centres: 6Kandhamal Zilla Sabuja Vaidya Sangathan (KZSVS)Daringbadi, Kandhamal, Odisha – 762104Contact: Dinabandhu Maharana, Founder & SecretaryEmail: kzsvs@yahoo.com | Phone: 7008810785  Concept Note for Pre-School Nut…Campaign tagline:“₹12 a Day. One Child. A Healthier Future.”
